es.term: OCT (prueba de tolerancia a la oxitocina)
aliases: prueba de tolerancia a la oxitocina
es.summary: Prueba de bienestar fetal que observa cómo responde la FCF a las contracciones uterinas, provocadas con oxitocina IV o estimulación del pezón. Busca detectar insuficiencia útero-placentaria.
key_points: Se necesitan al menos 3 contracciones de 40 segundos en 10 minutos.
Negativa (tranquilizadora): sin desaceleraciones tardías ni variables significativas.
Positiva (preocupante): desaceleraciones tardías en el 50 % o más de las contracciones.
Se indica si la NST es no reactiva o dudosa y no hay ultrasonido para un perfil biofísico.
Hoy se usa poco porque el perfil biofísico es menos invasivo.

purpose: Evaluar la reserva de oxígeno del feto: durante la contracción baja la oxigenación fetal.
Si el feto no tiene reserva, aparecen desaceleraciones tardías (DIP II).
procedure: Colocar el monitor externo de FCF y de contracciones.
Si no hay suficientes contracciones espontáneas, se usa estimulación del pezón u oxitocina IV según orden médica.
Registrar hasta lograr 3 contracciones de 40 segundos en 10 minutos.
Resultados: negativa, positiva, sospechosa, equívoca o insatisfactoria.
safety: Vigilar la taquisistolia y suspender la oxitocina si ocurre.
Tener a mano medidas de reanimación intrauterina: decúbito lateral, líquidos IV y oxígeno según protocolo.
nursing_care: Explicar la prueba y su motivo; obtener el consentimiento según la institución.
Colocar a la paciente en semi-Fowler o decúbito lateral para evitar la hipotensión supina.
Avisar de inmediato si la prueba es positiva.
documentation: Anotar hora de inicio y fin, método de estimulación (pezón u oxitocina y dosis), DU, línea de base de la FCF, desaceleraciones y resultado.

en.summary: A fetal well-being test that looks at how the FHR responds to uterine contractions, started with IV oxytocin or nipple stimulation (OCT in Spanish). It detects uteroplacental insufficiency.
key_points: The expected uterine contraction pattern for a CST is at least three contractions lasting for a minimum of 40 seconds each within a 10-minute period.
Negative: there are no late or significant variable decelerations.
Positive: late decelerations occur after 50 percent or more of contractions.
A CST may be recommended if the NST is nonreactive, or unclear, when ultrasound for a BPP is not available.
The CST is not widely used anymore due to the availability of a BPP, which is less invasive.

purpose: During contractions, there is a decrease in the oxygenation of the fetus.
If the fetus lacks a reserve of oxygen, late decelerations (DIP II) appear during contractions.
procedure: Apply the external fetal heart rate and contraction monitor.
If there are not enough spontaneous contractions, nipple stimulation or IV oxytocin is used as ordered.
Record until there are three 40-second contractions in 10 minutes.
Results: negative, positive, equivocal-suspicious, equivocal or unsatisfactory.
safety: Watch for tachysystole and stop the oxytocin if it occurs.
Be ready for intrauterine resuscitation: side-lying position, IV fluids and oxygen per protocol.
nursing_care: Explain the test and why it is done; obtain consent per facility policy.
Position the patient semi-Fowler or side-lying to avoid supine hypotension.
Notify the provider right away if the test is positive.
documentation: Record start and end times, stimulation method (nipple or oxytocin and dose), contractions, FHR baseline, decelerations and the result.

summary.0.quote: The health-care provider will order oxytocin (Pitocin) or have the pregnant person perform nipple stimulation to make their uterus contract.

summary.1.quote: If the fetus lacks a reserve of oxygen (demonstrating uteroplacental insufficiency), then a nonreassuring FHR pattern is noted during contractions (ACOG, 2021c).

key_points.0.quote: The expected uterine contraction pattern for a CST is at least three contractions lasting for a minimum of 40 seconds each within a 10-minute period.

key_points.1.quote: Negative: This means there are no late or significant variable decelerations ( Figure 13.11 ).

key_points.2.quote: Positive: Late decelerations occur after 50 percent or more of contractions, even if the contraction frequency is less than three in 10 minutes ( Figure 13.12 ).

key_points.3.quote: A contraction stress test (CST) may be recommended if the NST is nonreactive, or unclear, when ultrasound for a BPP is not available.

key_points.4.quote: The CST is not widely used anymore due to the availability of a BPP, which is less invasive.

sections.purpose.0.quote: During contractions, there is a decrease in the oxygenation of the fetus.

sections.purpose.1.quote: During a contraction, the decrease in oxygen to the fetus causes a deceleration that begins late in the contraction.

sections.procedure.0.quote: During this test, the external fetal and contraction monitor is applied.

sections.procedure.1.quote: However, if there are fewer than three contractions of 40 seconds each within 10 minutes, nipple stimulation or intravenous oxytocin will be used to induce contractions.

sections.procedure.2.quote: However, if there are fewer than three contractions of 40 seconds each within 10 minutes, nipple stimulation or intravenous oxytocin will be used to induce contractions.
